problem: "Each layer has exactly one job" contradicts the chapter's own layer list in Section 2, where the data link layer is given four jobs (framing, MAC addressing, error detection, medium access control) and the network layer three. A student can read this as a strict rule and then be confused when the same chapter lists several duties per layer.
fix: Each layer owns one group of related jobs — for example, the data link layer owns everything needed to move a frame across a single link — and serves the layer above it while being served by the layer below.

problem: "built it in the 1980s" is loose about the history: the work began in the late 1970s and the reference model was published as an ISO standard in 1984.
fix: Write: "Work on it began in the late 1970s and the reference model was published as an ISO standard in 1984, so that designers, vendors and teachers could talk about one layer at a time."

problem: "Keeping a user logged in across many requests" is ambiguous: in real software that is usually done by the application (cookies, tokens), so an examiner could mark either session or application.
fix: Reword the task so only one answer fits, e.g. "Deciding whose turn it is to speak in a long dialogue between two programs and inserting checkpoints so the transfer can resume after a break." (session)
